Prevention: Prune the tree to remove excess branches to allow light and air flow and to keep them at appropriate height for easy management.
Plant wind breakers around the mango orchard (live fencing of
Kei apple tree can be used) since wind accelerates the spread of the disease spores (powder).
Regular weeding of the field to reduce the likely infections in the field.
Monitoring: Look for a white powder on leaves, flowers, young fruits and twigs on a weekly basis.
Monitor the disease from new flush until flowering in the dry season.
Full bloom is the most vulnerable stage for powdery mildew in mango.
Control the disease upon appearance of the first symptoms.
Direct Control: Remove all infected fruits, leaves, flowers and twigs from the tree as soon as they are observed.
Spray the solution of 6 spoons of sodium bicarbonate (e.g. baking powder), 3 spoons of vegetable oil and white bar soap foam in 15
L of water on infected plants.
Spray entire tree with sulphur based pesticides (e.g.
Thiovit/ Thionil) at 40g/20L of water with 2 weeks.
Spray interval: from new flush tending to flowering until fruit set if infection confirmed.
